claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a 1930s hand-drawn cartoon art style and orchestral soundtrack.

citations.review_text: i beat this game in less than a week and i love it. the art, the animation, the soundtrack, the unique bosses, the storyline. i also like the 1930s aesthetic. i would say its worth the 20 bucks

A Masterpiece of Art, Gameplay, and Challenging Game Design!

Cuphead is an incredible example of how exceptional artistic design and carefully crafted gameplay can come together to create something truly special. From its stunning 1930s-inspired hand-drawn animations to its outstanding jazz soundtrack, every aspect of the game is bursting with creativity, personality, and attention to detail.

The gameplay is absolutely fantastic, with tight controls, responsive movement, and brilliantly designed boss fights that constantly test your reflexes, precision, and patience. Every encounter feels unique, introducing new attack patterns and mechanics that keep the experience fresh and exciting.

What I appreciate most about Cuphead is that it doesn't compromise its difficulty to appeal to everyone. This is a game designed for players who genuinely enjoy a challenge, and that's exactly what makes it so rewarding. Success requires practice, persistence, quick reactions, and mastering each boss's attack patterns. You will fail repeatedly, but every defeat teaches you something, making the eventual victory incredibly satisfying.

The difficulty can be brutal, but it rarely feels unfair. The game rewards skill and determination rather than holding your hand, something I wish more modern games would embrace.

The beautiful animations, imaginative character designs, incredible music, and challenging gameplay make Cuphead an unforgettable experience from beginning to end.

Cuphead is a brilliant reminder that games don't always need to be easy or accessible to everyone. Sometimes, overcoming a genuinely difficult challenge is exactly what makes gaming so enjoyable.

10/10 – A stunning artistic achievement and an absolute must-play for hardcore gamers who love a real challenge!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as heavily focused on boss fights where players must memorize attack patterns and repeat encounters multiple times.

citations.review_text:
Cupheads gameloop consists of self-contained levels that you try over and over from start, learning little bits and strategies with each attempt, until you eventually push through to the end. 85% of levels are essentially bossfights.

Whereas in most other games visual clutter would be considered bad design, in cuphead it is the game. The player has to manage the visual clutter (collision objects and background look largely identical) and the constant attacks and projectiles from all directions - while damaging the bosses.

Cuphead is about as difficult as dark souls 1 (albeit shorter, clocking in at around 15h for a regular playthrough of main + dlc). Your mom can't beat it, but you probably can.
There is an easy mode, but that actually cuts off the latter half of the encounters it seems. So technically your mom could probably beat it, but she would only see half the game. For that reason I would only recommend Cuphead to at least casual gamers.

this is an incredibly well made and good game. the only issue is that you have to hate yourself to enjoy it. i say issue very loosely because i know that i would not have it any other way. i strongly recommend this game to anyone except the following

- people who want a relaxing game. this game is the opposite of that. this game is the only game i still play that can make me rage

- people who are bad at videogames. if you are bad at videogames you should NOT buy this game. this is not some video game you can play as practice for other games and to make you better. if you don't know what you are doing this game will be a living hell. 

- people with no patience. you will have to fight every single boss over and over and over again to kill any of them. this is for more than one reason. the first being, this game is extremely hard. i can't over state how hard this is. and the second, if you don't have every single move for every single phase memorized, you will not be able to survive. you will die on every phase before you can memorize the move sets and kill the boss.

- people with anger issues. you WILL destroy your setup.

 -people with low dexterity. this game requires you to do so many things at once. you will need to press every button at once then switch to the ones you need when you need them by looking at the boss and using visual cues to determine what you need to do. if you are off by a second, a centimeter, or a button you die.

if you have or are any of these things DO NOT buy this game.

i strongly recommend

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as very difficult and challenging, often requiring multiple attempts to learn boss patterns.

citations.review_text: Very fun single player and multiplayer. Starts off hard but the more you play, the more you improve and it just gets more fun from there!

Cuphead

I hate this game.

10/10.

Cuphead is basically a beautiful 1930s cartoon that occasionally stops being art so it can beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of you.

Every boss starts the same way:

"Oh, this doesn't look too bad."

30 seconds later:

YOU DIED.

Again.

Again.

Again.

And then something weird happens.

You start recognizing the patterns.

You stop panic jumping.

You finally remember that pink things can be parried.

You get further than last time.

Then you die when the boss has approximately one molecule of HP left.

Fantastic. Love that for me.

The difficulty is brutal, but most of the time it feels fair. Every attempt teaches you something, and finally beating a boss that has been bullying you for the last 40 minutes feels genuinely satisfying.

The presentation is also ridiculous.

The hand-drawn animation is gorgeous, every boss has its own personality, the transformations are constantly creative, and the jazz soundtrack somehow makes getting murdered repeatedly feel classy.

Even the run-and-gun stages manage to be stressful enough to make me reconsider whether collecting one extra coin is worth my remaining sanity.

My only real warning is simple:

If repeating the same fight over and over until you memorize it sounds miserable, do not buy this.

Because that's the game.

For me though?

Apparently I enjoy suffering when it comes with good animation.
10/10

Beautiful. Creative. Addictive. Infuriating.

I have died to a cartoon flower more times than I am willing to admit

It's a game for masochists who enjoy putting themselves through hours of frustration just to feel good about finally beating some bosses.
There's a randomness to enemy attacks to make some attempts feel unfair. The parry mechanic can be inconsistent and sometimes will get in your way. For a game that demands pin point accuracy in certain bosses, its randomness makes certain hits difficult to avoid, forcing you to replay the same level over and over again until things work in your favor.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's cooperative mode as significantly harder than playing solo due to increased screen clutter, doubled hits, and longer boss phases.

citations.review_text:
Cuphead has an incredible art style that is as unique as visually appealing, and it combines it with amazing animations, sound design and music.
Gameplay is quick, easy to learn but satisfying to master, with a variety of interesting bosses and levels.

However it has one major flaw in my opinion.
It's a terrible shame that a game that is meant to be played in coop, is a thousand times better in every way when played solo. In coop you deal half as much damage making most boss phases a chore to get through (even though hits are doubled since there are 2 players, bosses take significantly longer); there are twice as many enemies in run and gun levels; and you can't both parry the same attack/object/enemy at the same time, making some boss phases near impossible such as Dice Man. That's not even talking about the significant difficulty added by visual clutter and having to revive your friend.
The game is often seriously infuriating, unfair and unfun when played as a duo, and I am not being dramatic. We played the entirety of the game in coop up until the Dice Man, had trouble beating him together, and I decided I'd give it a shot by myself. Beat him in 20 minutes tops. That's when I realized why would we go through the hassle and grind and suffer the bullshit when I can just have fun beating the boss by myself with an actually fair and balanced fight? I was seriously surprised at how fair the game felt when played by myself compared to coop.
We ended up giving up on beating Dice Man in coop and tried our luck against the Devil. Stupid idea. We gave up on that too as it was clear it would take hours of joyless grinding. I just did it by myself in under 15 minutes. Why does it seem so optimized AGAINST coop? That's so backwards.

Honestly if I only played Cuphead in solo, I would hold a very high opinion of it. Having played the majority of it in coop only to realise at the end how incredibly worse it is than solo, I am more lukewarm on the game. If you plan on playing b…

Definitely one of the toughest games I have played. The bosses are fun, and more importantly fair; Never once did I feel like I lost because the attack had some stupid range or AOE. Defeating the bosses always felt like an acomplishment.
Fun game overall, didn't drag, ended when I was growing a bit bored of the formula.

Must say though, definitely did not expect co-op to be harder, just the sheer amount of projectiles and moving objects of the screen overwhelm you and before you even know it both of you are on your last life. Had a blast beating a few bosses in co-op.

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that their computer, which can barely handle the resident evil remakes, had absolutely no problems with running it.

citation.review_text: With no glaze whatsoever, Cuphead might just be the perfect game. From the easily learned mechanics to the engaging playstyle, absolutely beautiful visuals and probably my favourite score of all time, Cuphead easily makes it to my favourite game probably of all time. Despite it's popularity and cute art, no matter how good you think you are, Cuphead is sure to be a devastanting challenge. Or maybe it just was for me, because I'm awful at platformers!! It was so hard but so, so rewarding- and the character designs are just so cute! From the great main characters+bosses to the quirky NPCs, every single character is so evidently designed with such care and love that it's impossible to not stop and try and talk to each one. I'm running out of praise, but I just want to say Cuphead is genuinely the most engaging game i have played to this date and the first game thus far that has enamoured me enough to wite a review. Plus, there's no reason not to get it- my computer, which can barely handle the resident evil remakes, had absolutely no problems with running it! It's only about 3GB in size.

Hardest game I've ever played, but worth it, all the way from the fast-paced bosses, to the extremely detailed and loveable characters, to the goofy but high-stakes storyline. Three cheers for The Inkwell Isles. They'll make you wanna kick The Devil's a$$!
